This enables: - Simpler position tracking - Better gap detection - Easier state persistence ### 3.7 Shuffle Algorithm **Chosen algorithm:** Fisher-Yates (Knuth) shuffle **Implementation:** ```rust pub fn shuffle_tracks(tracks: Vec, seed: u64) -> Vec { let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed); let mut indices: Vec = (0..tracks.len()).collect(); // Fisher-Yates: iterate backwards, swap with random earlier index for i in (1..indices.len()).rev() { let r = rng.gen_range(0..=i); indices.swap(i, r); } indices.into_iter().map(|i| tracks.remove(i)).collect() } ``` **Justification:** 1. **Uniform randomness:** Each permutation is equally likely (1/n!) 2. **O(n) time complexity:** Efficient for large queues 3. **Reproducible:** Given the same seed, produces identical order 4. **In-place:** Modifies the vector without allocation **Test vectors:** `data/shuffle_test_vectors.json` provides 8 test cases with known seeds and expected outputs. Caching Layer ### 4.1 Strategy Selection: LRU **Chosen strategy:** **LRU (Least Recently Used)** **Benchmark comparison** (from `benchmarks/cache_perf.json`): | Metric | LRU | LFU | ARC | |--------|-----|-----|-----| | Hit rate | **87.3%** | 82.1% | 89.7% | | Avg lookup | **45 ns** | 120 ns | 85 ns | | P99 lookup | **120 ns** | 340 ns | 210 ns | | Avg insert | 62 ns | 185 ns | 130 ns | | Avg eviction | **38 ns** | 95 ns | 72 ns | | Memory overhead | **2.1%** | 5.3% | 8.7% | | Prefetch improvement | 12.4% | 8.9% | 14.2% | **Why LRU over competitors:** | Comparison | Rationale | |------------|-----------| | LRU vs ARC | ARC has 4x higher memory overhead (8.7% vs 2.1%) and 2x slower lookups. Even though ARC has a 2.4% higher hit rate, the latency penalty and memory cost make it unsuitable for a mobile/embedded device context. Patent concerns on ARC (IBM) may also apply. | | LRU vs LFU | LFU performs worse for sequential access (78.4% vs 94.1% sequential hit rate) and has 3x higher overhead. Better suited for repeat-heavy workloads which are less common in music playback. | **Conclusion:** LRU provides the best trade-off between hit rate, lookup latency, and memory overhead. ### 4.2 Cache Configuration Default values from `config/cache_config.yaml`: ```yaml cache: strategy: LRU max_size_mb: 256 # ⚠️ DISCREPANCY: requirements.yaml says 512 MB prefetch_count: 3 eviction_policy: least_recently # ⚠️ DISCREPANCY: spelled with underscore vs text cache_dir: "~/.audio_player/cache" ttl_hours: 72 # ⚠️ DISCREPANCY: requirements.yaml says 168 hours ``` **Configuration parameters:** - `max_size_mb`: Maximum on-disk cache size - `prefetch_count`: Number of tracks to prefetch when current track reaches 75% - `eviction_policy`: "least_recently" (LRU) or "least_frequently" (LFU) - `ttl_hours`: Cache entry time-to-live (entries older than this are evicted) - `prefetch_trigger`: 75% of track duration (configurable) ### 4.3 Eviction Policy **LRU (Least Recently Used):** ```rust pub struct LruCache { inner: crate::lru::LruCache, // Maintains access order without explicit updates } ``` **LFU (Least Frequently Used) with aging:** ```rust pub struct LfuCache { frequency_map: HashMap, // When cache full, evict minimum frequency + time-based aging min_frequency_threshold: u64, min_age_seconds: u64, } ``` ### 4.4 Prefetch Behavior **Trigger condition:** When current track reaches 75% of its duration. **Action:** Prefetch next N tracks into cache. **Retry logic:** - If all N tracks already cached: no-op - If cache is full: evict least recently used entries to make room - If track decoding fails: skip to next track, retry on next 75% point ### 4.5 Cache Data Model **On-disk format:** Decoded PCM audio stored as memory-mapped files ``` Cache entry structure: ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Track UUID (blake3 hash) │ ← Cache key ├─────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Sample rate: u32 │ │ Channels: u8 │ │ Bit depth: u16 │ │ Duration: u64 │ │ PCM offset in file: u64 │ │ File size: u64 │ ├─────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Memory-mapped file (raw PCM samples)│ └─────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **File naming convention:** `.apcache` with content hash appended: `.apcache.blake3_` **Memory-mapped I/O:** Uses `memmap2` crate for efficient caching without copy-on-write overhead. ### 4.6 Cache Capacity Planning **Target:** 512 MB on-disk cache (configurable) **Track size distribution** (from `benchmarks/cache_perf.json`): - Mean: 8.5 MB - Std dev: 4.2 MB - Min: 0.5 MB - Max: 45.0 MB **Capacity calculation:** - Average tracks cacheable: 512 MB / 8.5 MB avg = ~60 tracks - With std dev, some prefixes may exceed limit (15-17 tracks for max variance cases) **In-memory footprint:** - The memory budget accounts for the LRU index only (~0.8 MB). ### 4.7 Cache Operations ```rust pub struct CacheStats { pub entry_count: usize, pub total_size_bytes: u64, pub hit_rate_last_100: f32, pub evictions_count: usize, pub total_prefetches: usize, } ``` ```rust pub struct CachePrefetchResult { pub track_id: String, pub result: CachePrefetchStatus, pub decode_duration_ms: u64, } #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)] pub enum CachePrefetchStatus { Success, SkippedAlreadyCached, Failed(String), } ``` ### 4.8 Benchmark Recommendations Based on `benchmarks/cache_perf.json`, configuration recommendations: - **Consumer devices (mobile/tablet):** `max_size_mb: 256` (hit rate 85%+) - **Desktop devices:** `max_size_mb: 512` (hit rate 88%+) - **High-latency environments:** Increase `prefetch_count` to 5 - **Memory-constrained devices:** Reduce `cache_index` to tuple-based LRU (0.3 MB index) --- ## 5.
